A1.justification: Both complete 56-page PDFs describe DSBench. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable matching of the main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–I.

before.justification: v2 reports original model and agent evaluations in Tables 4 and 6, human comparisons in Appendix B, and validation of the answer evaluator in Appendix F.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including the model and agent evaluations and the human evaluations in the appendices.

M1.justification: The benchmark procedures, agent inputs and outputs, and scoring methods are unchanged. Section 2.2.2 corrects N to A to match the training-set symbol already defined in both versions; this does not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 466 ModelOff data-analysis tasks and 74 Kaggle data-modeling tasks, with unchanged domains, modalities, and test scenarios.

E2.justification: The model, AutoGen, Code Interpreter, and human comparator rows in Tables 4, 6, and 8 are unchanged. Newly cited Spider 2.0 and DA-Code are related work, not additional evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The 8:2 Kaggle data split, evaluation metrics, model configurations, and human-evaluation sample sizes remain unchanged in Sections 2–3 and Appendices A, B, and F.

E4.justification: The input-length and release-time analyses in Figures 5–6 and Tables 5 and 7 are unchanged. Appendix F's evaluator validation and Appendices H–I's error analyses and case studies are also retained identically.

E5.justification: Appendix A still specifies greedy decoding and a single solution per instance. Neither version adds repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All reported numerical results and qualitative findings match. For example, AutoGen with GPT-4o retains 34.12% data-analysis accuracy in Table 4 and 34.74 RPG in Table 6; appendix results and example outputs are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The task definitions and RPG formula are unchanged in substance. Replacing N with A in Section 2.2.2 repairs notation to agree with the existing prose definition, without changing mathematical reasoning or introducing a new formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about DSBench's realism, the RPG metric, and the limitations of current data science agents.

C2.justification: Interpretations of context-length and release-time effects, human-performance gaps, and agent failures remain unchanged. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added.

D1.justification: Appendices A, C, and E retain the same model versions, hardware, prompts, input conversion, and execution details. The code and data access statement is also unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 4 adds Spider 2.0 (Lei et al., 2024) and DA-Code (Huang et al., 2024), with corresponding bibliography entries. This modestly expands related-work coverage without substantively revising DSBench's stated positioning.

P1.justification: Limited edits expand the related-work list, correct the training-input symbol in Section 2.2.2, and update the arXiv version/date stamp. Section organization and the remaining exposition are unchanged.

P2.justification: The added citations produce limited paragraph reflow on page 10 and redistribute bibliography entries across pages 12–15. Figures, tables, and all appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves clarity by aligning the task formula with its defined training input and improves related-work completeness by citing Spider 2.0 and DA-Code. These limited gains do not alter the experimental evidence, analyses, or conclusions.
